title: Phosphorus and Sulphur
notes: **Phosphorus allotropes:** white P (waxy, poisonous, $P_4$ tetrahedron, glows in dark), red P (amorphous, stable, non-toxic), black P (layered, conductor, most stable).

**Phosphine ($PH_3$):** prepared by reacting calcium phosphide with acid: $Ca_3P_2 + 6HCl \rightarrow 3CaCl_2 + 2PH_3$. Toxic, flammable, basic (turns red litmus blue), reducing agent (turns $CuSO_4$ solution brown).
**Sulphur allotropes:** rhombic ($S_8$ rings, stable below 95.5°C), monoclinic (stable 95.5-119°C), plastic (long chains, elastic).

**$H_2S$:** weak acid, strong reducing agent, poisonous rotten egg smell. Prepared by Kipp's apparatus: $FeS + 2HCl \rightarrow FeCl_2 + H_2S$. Forms black precipitate with lead acetate: $Pb(CH_3COO)_2 + H_2S \rightarrow PbS + 2CH_3COOH$.
**$SO_2$:** acidic, reducing (turns acidified $K_2Cr_2O_7$ from orange to green), oxidising (with $H_2S$), bleaching agent (temporary, restores colour on standing).
**$H_2SO_4$ (conc.):** dehydrating agent (chars sugar), oxidising (with Cu: $Cu + 2H_2SO_4 \rightarrow CuSO_4 + SO_2 + 2H_2O$), non-volatile (used to prepare volatile acids).
